note: The open-source tools the reality check runs as contestants and as part bake-off baselines. EVERY ONE IS PINNED: Python tools by a hash-locked requirements file made with `uv pip compile --generate-hashes --exclude-newer 2026-10-13` (so nothing in the tree is younger than two weeks), installed with `uv pip sync --require-hashes`; npm tools by an exact version and the package-lock.json beside it (`npm ci`). Nothing is fetched at run time: an agent that downloads a plugin or a model price list fails closed (no CA bundle, no proxy variables, a throwaway HOME). Tools live in e2e/cache/tools (git-ignored); `npm run e2e:tools -- install <name...>` makes them, `verify` checks each reports its pinned version, `licences` lists the licence of every installed Python package. None of this code is vendored into the product: each tool is a separate process, started from a scrubbed environment.
supplyChain: LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on PyPI carried an infostealer (24 March 2026). aider pins litellm==1.81.10; mini-swe-agent is constrained to the same; OpenHands needs litellm>=1.83.7 and resolves 1.105.0 (uploaded 2026-10-11, older than the two-week floor). No tool uses @latest.

aider.licenceNote: Run as a separate process; nothing vendored. Of its 108 installed Python dependencies none is GPL or LGPL; four are MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft: certifi, orjson, pathspec, tqdm), which is fine for a program we only run. In maintenance mode upstream (last release 0.86.2, February 2026).
aider.installCmd: uv venv --python 3.12 e2e/cache/tools/aider && uv pip sync --python e2e/cache/tools/aider/bin/python --require-hashes e2e/agents/locks/aider.txt

mini-swe-agent.licenceNote: Separate process. Of its 74 installed Python dependencies none is GPL or LGPL; two are MPL-2.0 (certifi, tqdm). litellm held at 1.81.10 (see supplyChain).
mini-swe-agent.installCmd: uv venv --python 3.12 e2e/cache/tools/mini-swe-agent && uv pip sync --python e2e/cache/tools/mini-swe-agent/bin/python --require-hashes e2e/agents/locks/mini-swe-agent.txt

openhands.licenceNote: OpenHands CLI and SDK are MIT. Two of its 207 transitive Python dependencies are strong copyleft: bashlex (GPL-3.0-or-later) and func_timeout (LGPL-2); four more are MPL-2.0. They are imported by the OpenHands process itself, which is started as a separate program from a throwaway home; they are not installed in our Node tree, not linked into or copied into our code, and nothing of OpenHands is redistributed. Do not bundle this venv into any image we ship.
openhands.headless: works without Docker: `openhands --headless --override-with-envs --json -t <task>` runs the agent in-process on a local workspace (verified 2026-10-27). `requiresDocker` is therefore false.
openhands.installCmd: uv venv --python 3.12 e2e/cache/tools/openhands && uv pip sync --python e2e/cache/tools/openhands/bin/python --require-hashes e2e/agents/locks/openhands.txt

trafilatura.licenceNote: Apache-2.0 since 1.8.0 (earlier releases were GPL-3.0: never pin below 1.8). Used as a library inside a separate Python process that reads saved pages; one transitive package, tld, is multi-licensed (MPL-1.1 OR GPL-2.0-only OR LGPL-2.1-or-later) and is taken under MPL-1.1.
trafilatura.installCmd: uv venv --python 3.12 e2e/cache/tools/trafilatura && uv pip sync --python e2e/cache/tools/trafilatura/bin/python --require-hashes e2e/agents/locks/trafilatura.txt

codex.licenceNote: Prebuilt Rust binary from the @openai/codex-linux-x64 package; run directly (not through the npm launcher), as a separate process. Speaks the Responses API only (`wire_api = "chat"` is refused), so the proxy translates /v1/responses (adapters/responses.ts).
codex.installCmd: cp e2e/agents/locks/node-codex/* e2e/cache/tools/codex/ && npm ci --prefix e2e/cache/tools/codex --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund

opencode.licenceNote: Prebuilt binary from the opencode-linux-x64 package, installed with --ignore-scripts and run directly. Always started with --pure (no external plugins are installed at run time) and a single OPENCODE_CONFIG that names our proxy as an openai-compatible provider.
opencode.installCmd: cp e2e/agents/locks/node-opencode/* e2e/cache/tools/opencode/ && npm ci --prefix e2e/cache/tools/opencode --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund

garak.role: security probe source (NVIDIA garak): NOT installed here
garak.licenceNote: Running it as a separate scanner is fine. Not installed in this container: it requires torch>=2.13, transformers, datasets and litellm>=1.84 (several GB; this disk has about 5). e2e/security/garak.ts therefore carries a small probe set in garak's own shapes (promptinject, latentinjection, dan, encoding) and scores with garak's detectors' idea (a trigger string in the output); the full tool is wired as `npm run e2e:security -- --garak-cmd`.
garak.installCmd: uv venv --python 3.12 e2e/cache/tools/garak && uv pip install --python e2e/cache/tools/garak/bin/python garak==0.17.0 (needs ~6 GB free; unpinned transitive dependencies: lock them first with uv pip compile --generate-hashes --exclude-newer 2026-10-13)

nodeDevDependencies.note: Page extraction baselines, in tulmi/package.json devDependencies at exact versions (npm ci --omit=dev leaves them out of the image). They are loaded only by e2e/bakeoff/extract.ts.

publicBenchmarks.note: Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench Pro run their tasks in Docker containers; this container has the docker CLI but no daemon, so they are documented (e2e/README.md) and skipped here. Harbor (Apache-2.0) is the runner.
